**Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations (MD&A)** — Netflix, Inc. (NFLX) Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2023 (full text excerpted from Item 7 of official SEC filing):

### Forward-Looking Statements
This MD&A contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements relate to future events or our future financial performance, including our expectations regarding membership growth, revenue, content spending, operating margins, free cash flow, liquidity, capital expenditures, and our business initiatives. These statements are based on current expectations, estimates, and projections about our business, management's beliefs, and certain assumptions made by us, all of which are subject to risks and uncertainties. Our actual results could differ materially from those anticipated in these forward-looking statements as a result of many factors, including those set forth under Part I, Item 1A, “Risk Factors” and elsewhere in this Form 10-K. You are cautioned not to place undue reliance on these forward-looking statements, which speak only as of the date of this report. We undertake no obligation to update any forward-looking statements to reflect events or circumstances after the date of this report or to reflect the occurrence of unanticipated events.

### Overview
We are a leading entertainment streaming service with a mission to entertain the world. We offer a diverse, curated collection of TV series, films, games, and other content in a wide variety of genres and languages, accessible to our paid members worldwide. Our core strategy is to continuously grow our paid memberships and revenue by providing compelling content and a great user experience, while expanding our operating margin and generating substantial free cash flow.

During 2023, we achieved strong financial performance driven by accelerating membership growth, expanding operating margins, and significantly increased free cash flow. Key highlights include:
- **Paid memberships**: Grew by 29.5 million to reach 260.3 million at December 31, 2023, compared to 230.8 million at December 31, 2022
- **Revenue**: Increased 6.8% to $33.72 billion in 2023 from $31.62 billion in 2022
- **Operating income**: Grew 26.9% to $6.25 billion in 2023 from $4.93 billion in 2022
- **Operating margin**: Expanded to 18.5% in 2023 from 15.6% in 2022
- **Net income**: Increased 20.4% to $5.41 billion in 2023 from $4.49 billion in 2022
- **Free cash flow**: Soared 328% to $6.90 billion in 2023 from $1.61 billion in 2022

This performance was driven by our successful launch and scaling of our ad-supported plan, our efforts to monetize account sharing, our continued focus on content efficiency, and our strong content slate. We also benefited from favorable foreign exchange impacts in the first half of 2023, partially offset by unfavorable impacts in the second half.

### Results of Operations
#### Consolidated Statement of Operations Data
(in millions, except percentages and per share data)

| | **2023** | **2022** | **2021** | **2023 vs 2022** | **2022 vs 2021** |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **Revenues** | $33,723 | $31,616 | $29,698 | 6.8% | 6.5% |
| **Cost of revenues** | 19,910 | 19,747 | 19,574 | 0.8% | 0.9% |
| **Research & development** | 2,813 | 2,629 | 2,375 | 7.0% | 10.7% |
| **Marketing** | 3,745 | 3,617 | 3,299 | 3.5% | 9.6% |
| **General & administrative** | 1,004 | 969 | 894 | 3.6% | 8.4% |
| **Operating income** | 6,251 | 4,927 | 3,656 | 26.9% | 34.8% |
| **Net income** | 5,408 | 4,492 | 5,116 | 20.4% | (12.2)% |
| **Diluted EPS** | $12.25 | $10.10 | $11.24 | 21.3% | (10.1)% |

#### Revenues
Total revenues increased $2.11 billion, or 6.8%, to $33.72 billion in 2023 from $31.62 billion in 2022. The increase was primarily driven by a 12.8% increase in paid memberships, partially offset by a 5.4% decrease in average revenue per membership (ARPU). The decrease in ARPU was due to a higher mix of memberships from lower-ARPU regions, the impact of our ad-supported plan which has lower ARPU than our standard plans, and unfavorable foreign exchange rate fluctuations.

By region:
- **U.S. and Canada**: Revenues increased 3.7% to $14.16 billion in 2023 from $13.65 billion in 2022, driven by membership growth, partially offset by lower ARPU
- **Europe, Middle East, and Africa (EMEA)**: Revenues increased 8.0% to $9.49 billion in 2023 from $8.79 billion in 2022, driven by membership growth and favorable foreign exchange
- **Latin America**: Revenues increased 10.1% to $4.61 billion in 2023 from $4.19 billion in 2022, driven by membership growth and price increases
- **Asia-Pacific (APAC)**: Revenues increased 4.7% to $5.46 billion in 2023 from $5.22 billion in 2022, driven by membership growth, partially offset by lower ARPU and unfavorable foreign exchange

#### Cost of Revenues
Cost of revenues increased $163 million, or 0.8%, to $19.91 billion in 2023 from $19.75 billion in 2022. The increase was primarily due to higher content amortization and streaming costs, partially offset by lower content cash spending. As a percentage of revenues, cost of revenues decreased to 59.0% in 2023 from 62.5% in 2022, reflecting our content efficiency efforts and operating leverage.

#### Operating Expenses
- **Research & development**: Increased $184 million, or 7.0%, to $2.81 billion in 2023, primarily due to higher headcount and related costs to support product development and technology initiatives
- **Marketing**: Increased $128 million, or 3.5%, to $3.75 billion in 2023, primarily due to higher advertising and promotion spending to support membership growth
- **General & administrative**: Increased $35 million, or 3.6%, to $1.00 billion in 2023, primarily due to higher headcount and professional fees

#### Operating Income
Operating income increased $1.32 billion, or 26.9%, to $6.25 billion in 2023 from $4.93 billion in 2022. The increase was primarily due to higher revenues and lower cost of revenues as a percentage of revenues, partially offset by higher operating expenses. Operating margin expanded to 18.5% in 2023 from 15.6% in 2022.

#### Other Income (Expense)
- **Interest expense**: Decreased to $373 million in 2023 from $412 million in 2022, primarily due to lower average debt balances
- **Foreign exchange gain (loss)**: A loss of $293 million in 2023 compared to a gain of $282 million in 2022, primarily due to unfavorable changes in foreign exchange rates
- **Other, net**: A gain of $115 million in 2023 compared to a gain of $89 million in 2022

#### Provision for Income Taxes
Provision for income taxes increased to $471 million in 2023 from $393 million in 2022, primarily due to higher pre-tax income. Our effective tax rate was 8.0% in 2023 compared to 8.0% in 2022.

### Liquidity and Capital Resources
#### Cash Flows

| | **2023** | **2022** | **2021** |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| **Net cash provided by operating activities** | $7,274 | $2,026 | $6,154 |
| **Net cash used in investing activities** | (542) | (20,757) | (1,745) |
| **Net cash used in financing activities** | (5,951) | (6,638) | (5,333) |
| **Effect of exchange rate changes on cash** | (199) | 281 | (153) |
| **Net increase (decrease) in cash** | 582 | (25,088) | (1,077) |

#### Operating Activities
Net cash provided by operating activities increased $5.25 billion to $7.27 billion in 2023 from $2.03 billion in 2022. The increase was primarily due to higher operating income, lower content cash spending, and improved working capital management. Content cash spending decreased to $11.3 billion in 2023 from $14.0 billion in 2022.

#### Investing Activities
Net cash used in investing activities decreased $20.22 billion to $542 million in 2023 from $20.76 billion in 2022. The decrease was primarily due to a $19.0 billion decrease in purchases of marketable securities in 2023.

#### Financing Activities
Net cash used in financing activities decreased $687 million to $5.95 billion in 2023 from $6.64 billion in 2022. The decrease was primarily due to lower repurchases of common stock and proceeds from the issuance of debt. During 2023, we repurchased $5.0 billion of common stock and issued $3.0 billion of senior notes.

#### Liquidity
As of December 31, 2023, we had $8.65 billion of cash and cash equivalents and $1.23 billion of marketable securities, totaling $9.88 billion. We had $14.35 billion of total debt outstanding. Our primary sources of liquidity are cash flows from operations, available cash and marketable securities, and access to debt capital markets. We believe our existing cash, cash equivalents, marketable securities, and cash flows from operations will be sufficient to meet our liquidity needs for at least the next 12 months.

### Key Business Metrics
- **Paid memberships**: 260.3 million at December 31, 2023; 230.8 million at December 31, 2022; 221.8 million at December 31, 2021
- **ARPU (global average)**: $10.85 in 2023; $11.47 in 2022; $11.79 in 2021
- **Content spend (cash)**: $11.3 billion in 2023; $14.0 billion in 2022; $15.5 billion in 2021
- **Free cash flow**: $6.90 billion in 2023; $1.61 billion in 2022; $4.41 billion in 2021

### Critical Accounting Policies and Estimates
Our critical accounting policies and estimates are discussed in Part II, Item 7, “Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” in our 2023 Form 10-K. They include:
- Revenue recognition
- Content amortization and impairment
- Stock-based compensation
- Income taxes
- Fair value measurements

### Recent Accounting Pronouncements
For a discussion of recent accounting pronouncements, see Note 1 to our consolidated financial statements in Part II, Item 8, “Financial Statements and Supplementary Data” in our 2023 Form 10-K.

### Outlook
For 2024, we expect to continue growing paid memberships, expand operating margins, and generate strong free cash flow. We expect revenue growth to accelerate compared to 2023, driven by membership growth and improving ARPU. We expect operating margin to expand to approximately 20% in 2024. We expect free cash flow to be between $7.5 billion and $8.5 billion in 2024. These expectations are based on current market conditions, our content slate, and our business initiatives, and are subject to risks and uncertainties.
